HOME INSPECTION REPORT BUILDER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Write a clear home inspection report in minutes

Add findings from a library of plain-language comments, edit the wording, set severity, add your own notes and repair cost ranges, then print a report sorted with safety and major items first. Save your work to a file on your own device and load it later.

A writing aid for working inspectors. You are responsible for every statement in the report.

Questions people ask

Is there a free alternative to paid home inspection report software?

This tool builds a printable report from a library of editable comments with no account and no subscription. It does not replace a full inspection platform with photos, scheduling and agreements, but it covers the core job of turning your findings into a clear, severity-sorted report.

Where does my data go?

Nowhere. Everything stays in your browser. Save your report to a file on your own device and load it later; the page does not store it for you.

Does the comment library follow a standard of practice?

No. The wording is generic and is a starting point for you to edit. It does not cite or apply any code, standard of practice or licensing rule. You decide what to report and how, and you are responsible for the final report.

Can I add my own comments?

Yes. Add a custom finding with your own title, wording, severity and recommendation, or edit any library comment after adding it.

Not decided

What a home inspection must cover, which standard of practice or licensing rules apply where you work, what is a defect at a particular property, repair costs (the ranges are your own figures, not a measurement), and the legal wording of your inspection agreement. The library is generic starting text, not a statement of any standard.

Related tools: the property tax appeal calculator, the security deposit return calculator and the fix and flip deal analyzer.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, accounting, compliance, or financial advice, and it does not replace a qualified advisor. You are responsible for reviewing and verifying its output before relying on it, and for meeting any licensing, standard-of-practice, disclosure or contract obligation that applies to your inspection. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors accept no liability for any loss or damage arising from its use.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record — nothing you enter is saved anywhere by this tool; use the save-to-file button to keep your work.

Everything runs in your browser. Your answers are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (report_built, finding_added) are counted only in local storage on your device. The counts can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

If this helped you, you can sponsor the project on GitHub. It stays free either way.
